NASA Space Apps 2026 Synaptic

Earth System Trend Detective · 2026

An AI research harness for Earth science

Synaptic searched NASA satellite records and found three changes we could not find in any published paper. Every test was written down before its data were downloaded, and code, not an agent, decided the result.

New measurements and re-tested trends

Our NASA ADS search found no published measurements matching three results from Synaptic’s investigations: northern Morocco’s winter recharge, the UAE’s shift in weekly nitrogen dioxide, and Lake Chad’s 2024 water storage gain. A separate investigation re-tested three published river-mouth chlorophyll trends using a different satellite and time period.

#1 Morocco#2 UAE#3 Lake Chad#4 River re-test

#1 Northern Morocco

Satellites measured Morocco’s rebound from drought

Confirmed by a second satellite (SMAP)

17–21 km³more water stored than in a typical winter

Northern Morocco stored substantially more water than usual after the rains of winter 2025–26.

How we checked itTwo GRACE estimates gave the storage range. A preregistered SMAP test independently confirmed unusually wet topsoil (p = 0.011).

#2 United Arab Emirates

A new weekend reshaped the weekly pollution cycle

Confirmed · pre-registered test, control cities show nothing

24%lower Sunday nitrogen dioxide after the 2022 shift, relative to a working day

After the UAE changed its weekend, Dubai and Abu Dhabi went from having their lowest nitrogen dioxide levels on Fridays to having them on Sundays.

How we checked itA preregistered test of 22 years of daily Aura OMI data found the shift (p = 0.00005), while four control cities showed no shift on that date.

#3 Lake Chad basin

Lake Chad’s record rains left a record water gain

Measured on two GRACE solutions · second-satellite check not significant

≈75 km³extra water stored during the 2024 rainy season

The 2024 rainy season brought the largest water storage gain around Lake Chad in the GRACE record since 2003.

How we checked itTwo GRACE processing teams found a similar gain. The independent SMAP soil moisture check did not reach significance (p = 0.10).

#4 U.S. river mouths

Three published trends did not reappear in the re-test

Re-test · not detected (p = 0.37–0.43)

0 of 3published chlorophyll trends detected in the MODIS re-test

We did not detect the chlorophyll trends previously reported for two Mississippi sites and one Eel River site.

How we checked itTwo implementations agreed after accounting for month-to-month carry-over in MODIS Aqua data from 2002–2025 (p = 0.37–0.43). The original study used a different sensor and period.

Reproduce every finding offline with python -m synaptic reproduce. The code, data and pre-registered tests are in the GitHub repository.

How it works

Agents propose. Code decides.

Synaptic runs a research group of NVIDIA Nemotron agents. They can explore NASA data, form hypotheses and review each other, but none of them can promote its own claim.

01

Agents propose

A planner, a principal investigator, workers and supervisors who read the raw numbers and charts, referees and an auditor.

02

Written down first

Every confirmation test is saved to git before its data are downloaded: dataset, region, months and threshold.

03

Code decides

Code runs the test on data no agent can read. Agents can lower a verdict, never raise it.

The proof is on GitHubCode, every pre-registered test with its results, the evidence bundles and one command that recomputes every number.

The challenge app

Trend Detective: an honest answer in five steps

  1. Variable: 41 NASA datasets in plain words, including MODIS, OMI, AIRS, GPM, MERRA-2, GLDAS and GRACE.
  2. Region: any country, US state, box or the whole world.
  3. Period: any years and any season.
  4. Time series: yearly and monthly, plus a map of where it changes.
  5. Significance: tests that account for year-to-year memory, with the verdict in plain words.

The challenge video’s own example: summer smoke over Wisconsin has no significant long-term trend (p = 0.31), but 2023–2025 sit clearly above it (p = 0.006), the Canadian wildfire years. The app runs on your computer with python -m synaptic dashboard; setup is on GitHub.

What we refused to claim

Most ideas failed. We report all of them.

“Not shown” means the test was not significant. It is never reported as “refuted”, and never hidden.

  • Not shown

    More water stored than rain minus evaporation explains.

  • Not shown

    Slower draining than usual, and a darker desert surface afterwards.

  • Not shown

    14 long-term drifts across Africa, tested on years no agent had seen.

  • 0 of 5

    Worldwide scan of 1,534 block-seasons: five record candidates, none confirmed.

  • Not relied on

    Oman and Saudi weekend tests passed, but a control city moved too.

  • Caught

    Twice the system called a textbook result “new”. We caught it, fixed the check and logged it.
